This case presents a classic phenotypic and biochemical profile of non–salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase deficiency congenital adrenal hyperplasia (21-OHD CAH). The genital ambiguity at birth (clitoromegaly + partial labial fusion) is pathognomonic for prenatal virilization due to fetal adrenal androgen excess — the hallmark of classic 21-OHD. Postnatal manifestations — primary amenorrhea and severe acne — reflect persistent postnatal androgen excess from uncontrolled adrenal hyperplasia. Biochemically, the markedly elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone (145 ng/dL; normal <2 ng/dL in non-stressed individuals, and >10–20 ng/dL highly suggestive of classic 21-OHD even without stimulation) is the single most specific diagnostic marker. Elevated androstenedione further supports adrenal origin of androgens. Crucially, preserved renin (normal PRA) and aldosterone exclude mineralocorticoid deficiency — confirming the non–salt-wasting (simple virilizing) variant. Morning cortisol is normal but likely reflects compensatory HPA axis activation; it does not rule out impaired cortisol reserve, which is why ACTH stimulation is indicated. Maternal virilization during pregnancy is a well-recognized clue: maternal exposure to fetal adrenal androgens (via placental transfer of weak androgens or possibly 17-OHP) can cause transient maternal hirsutism — supporting intrauterine androgen excess. The bone fragility is a plausible long-term complication due to chronic anovulation → estrogen deficiency → impaired bone accrual, compounded by possible suboptimal glucocorticoid replacement history or intrinsic effects of hyperandrogenemia on bone metabolism.

[EVIDENCE]  
- Clitoromegaly and partial labial fusion at birth → prenatal androgen excess  
- Primary amenorrhea → chronic anovulation due to hyperandrogenemia and disrupted HPO axis  
- Severe acne → postnatal androgen excess  
- Serum 17-OHP = 145 ng/dL → diagnostic-level elevation for classic 21-hydroxylase deficiency  
- Serum androstenedione = 8.2 ng/mL → elevated, consistent with adrenal androgen overproduction  
- Normal plasma renin activity (1.8 ng/mL/hr) → excludes salt-wasting physiology  
- Normal aldosterone (8.2 ng/dL) → excludes mineralocorticoid deficiency  
- Maternal virilization (chin hair) during pregnancy → indirect evidence of fetal androgen excess crossing placenta

- ACTH stimulation test results (baseline and peak 17-OHP/cortisol) — pending; needed to confirm impaired cortisol reserve and diagnostic specificity  
- Serum electrolytes (Na⁺, K⁺), blood pressure, and clinical volume status — not specified; required to definitively exclude subtle salt-wasting

- Estradiol and FSH/LH levels — not reported; critical to characterize gonadotropin status and degree of HPO axis suppression  
- Bone mineral density (DXA) result — noted as warranted but not yet obtained; needed to quantify skeletal involvement  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Classic 21-Hydroxylase Deficiency Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (Simple Virilizing Variant)
